clue.text: Channel without water, do we hear?

indicators.note: asking what we hear points to a word that is spoken, not spelt, so the sound matters here

blocks.note: a spirit taken straight is drunk neat, with no water added

explanation.surface: Someone checks they have caught the name of a dry channel correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: A drink served straight has nothing mixed in; the sea channel sounds the same but is spelt STRAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow passage of sea joining two larger bodies of water, such as the one at Dover.

clue.text: Rose's companion is an old character

blocks.note: first meaning: the prickle that grows on a rose stem, as in no rose without one
second meaning: a runic letter used in Old English for the th sound

explanation.surface: A woman called Rose has a friend who is a bit of an eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: Rose reads as a woman's name and character as a person; THORN is the old letter þ, still used in Icelandic.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorns accompany every rose stem, and thorn is also the name of an old runic letter written þ.

clue.text: Tree-garden a right tedious experience to little Mary

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the usual abbreviation for right
something tedious is a bore
little Mary is old British slang for the stomach

explanation.surface: A garden of trees proves a dull outing for a small girl called Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Mary is not a child: it is a dated British nickname for the stomach, from a J. M. Barrie play.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a botanical collection of living trees, planted and kept for study or display.

clue.text: Gold they received from speculation

indicators.note: what is received is taken in, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Speculators were paid in gold for their gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is heraldry's word for gold, a staple of crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is an idea not yet proven, a supposition, which is what speculation produces.

clue.text: No latecomers on this list

blocks.note: surface reading: a register from which anyone arriving late has been struck off
setter's reading: whoever runs on this timetable is, by the idiom, never late

explanation.surface: A strict guest list bars anyone who turns up late.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone 'on schedule' is on time, so a list whose people are on it has no latecomers.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule is a timetable or list of planned times, and keeping to it means arriving punctually.

clue.text: Deputy Ivan got nothing, oddly, in public acclaim

indicators.note: doing something oddly means doing it in a strange way, so the letters are put in an unusual order

blocks.note: a deputy stands in for someone
taken as written
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A deputy named Ivan behaved strangely and came away empty-handed when publicly praised.
explanation.definitionFit: When an audience rises to its feet to applaud, that is the warmest form of public acclaim.

clue.text: Browning's Evelyn accepts mince pies for help in the garden

indicators.note: to mince is to chop finely, so these letters are cut up and reassembled
accepting something means taking it in, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: Evelyn Hope is the title of a Robert Browning poem
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet's character bakes mince pies to keep the gardeners going.
explanation.walkthrough: Mince pies are a British Christmas pastry, but here mince is a verb. Browning's poem Evelyn Hope supplies the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A hosepipe carries water to plants and lawns, a practical tool for anyone tending a garden.

clue.text: 500 only raised in the island

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it bottom to top, reversing it

blocks.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: Only five hundred people were brought up on some island.
explanation.definitionFit: Delos is a small Greek island in the Cyclades, mythical birthplace of Apollo and Artemis.

clue.text: Sea-food cooked along with suet

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters come out in a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seafood dish has been prepared with suet in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A langouste is a spiny lobster, a shellfish served in restaurants as a seafood delicacy.

clue.text: Instrument makes fish run in front

indicators.note: placing one part in front tells us the order in which the two parts are joined

blocks.note: to double is to run, as soldiers do at the double
a bass is a fish

explanation.surface: An instrument is made from a fish, with a run at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: At the double is military jargon for running, so double can mean run.
explanation.definitionFit: The double bass is the largest bowed string instrument of the orchestra, played upright.

clue.text: Cat seen in chains, say?

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the word, so its sound counts and not its spelling

blocks.note: chains are made of links

explanation.surface: A big cat is spotted wearing chains.
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx is a wild member of the feline family, with tufted ears and a short tail.

clue.text: Find trouble about uncommon type of radiation

indicators.note: trouble here is a verb, so the letters are disturbed into a new order
about means around, so the first piece wraps round the second

blocks.note: taken as written
rare means uncommon

explanation.surface: Someone runs into problems with an unusual kind of radiation.
explanation.definitionFit: Infra-red radiation lies just beyond visible red light in the spectrum and is felt as heat.

clue.text: Ancient Shakespearian weapon

blocks.note: first meaning: Falstaff's swaggering ensign, called an ancient, in Henry IV and Henry V
second meaning: a handgun

explanation.surface: An old weapon from Shakespeare's time.
explanation.walkthrough: Ancient looks like 'very old', but it is the old army rank of ensign, held by Shakespeare's character.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's braggart Pistol holds the rank of ancient, and a pistol is also a small firearm.

clue.text: March with brass instrument in retreat

indicators.note: an army in retreat goes back the way it came, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a tuba is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: A military band marches, then falls back carrying its brass.
explanation.walkthrough: March here is the noun for a border, so to march with is to share a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: Lands that march with each other share a border, and abut likewise means lie adjacent or touch.

clue.text: Giving Keats perpetual joy

blocks.note: surface reading: something that made the poet happy for ever
setter's reading: Keats wrote that a thing of beauty is a joy for ever, so this describes such a thing

explanation.surface: Something brought the poet lasting happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening line of Keats's Endymion is 'A thing of beauty is a joy for ever'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Keats's famous line it is a thing of beauty that remains a joy for ever, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: Family preference for some wine-pot is manifest

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across wine-pot, is and manifest

explanation.surface: A family prefers some wine from a pot, plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouritism shown to relatives, especially in handing out jobs or power.

clue.text: Stage performer is extremely noisy

blocks.note: surface reading: a complaint about an actor who shouts too much
setter's reading: a performer whose feet make the noise, the extremities of the body

explanation.surface: An actor on stage is far too loud.
explanation.walkthrough: Extremely hints at the extremities: this performer is noisy at the feet, with metal plates on the shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap-dancer wears shoes with metal plates and makes rhythmic clicking sounds while performing on stage.

clue.text: Request to turn over to the state bad food product

blocks.note: PTO, please turn over, is written at the foot of a page
Maine is a US state

explanation.surface: Someone asks for something bad to be handed over to the state.
explanation.walkthrough: The state is a specific American state, not government.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptomaines are compounds produced when protein rots, once blamed for food poisoning, so a product of bad food.

clue.text: Tree top, metal construction

indicators.note: a construction is something built up, so these letters are assembled anew

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The top of a tree is made of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A palmetto is a fan-leaved palm tree native to the south-eastern United States.

clue.text: King of Spain quietly goes ahead to the quarry

indicators.note: going ahead means coming first, so this piece leads the other

blocks.note: p, piano, means quietly in music
rey is Spanish for king

explanation.surface: The Spanish king walks softly on ahead towards the hunted animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarry is the animal being hunted, which is exactly what prey means.

clue.text: One hiring Holmes was illustrious but anonymous

definitions.text: One hiring Holmes was illustrious but anonymous

blocks.clueFragment: One hiring Holmes was illustrious but anonymous
blocks.note: surface reading: a famous person secretly employed the detective

blocks.clueFragment: One hiring Holmes was illustrious but anonymous
blocks.note: setter's reading: the Conan Doyle story about a nameless, distinguished customer of the detective

explanation.surface: A famous person secretly employed Sherlock Holmes.
explanation.walkthrough: In Conan Doyle's The Adventure of the Illustrious Client the person paying Holmes is never named.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who engages a detective's services is that detective's customer, the person paying for the work.

clue.text: The flower of our schoolchildren

definitions.note: a stream is one ability group of schoolchildren, not all of them

blocks.note: first meaning: crossword code for something that flows, a small river
second meaning: in British schools pupils are sorted by ability into groups with this name

explanation.surface: The brightest and best of the nation's pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: The flower of reads as 'the finest of', but flower is crossword code for a river, something that flows. British schools 'stream' pupils, sorting them into ability groups.
explanation.definitionFit: A brook is something that flows, and in British schools a class grouped by ability shares the same name.

clue.text: Antelope is one right from the Emerald Isle

indicators.note: taking something from a word removes those letters from it

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
R is short for right
the Emerald Isle is a nickname for Ireland

explanation.surface: A single antelope has come from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing I and R from IRELAND leaves the antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope with spiral horns, the biggest of its kind.

clue.text: Marriage, if caught - all that is put outside

indicators.note: placing something outside means it goes round the other pieces

blocks.note: taken as written
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
an is an archaic word for if, as in Shakespeare
c is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A wedding happens only if everyone is caught and thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: An meaning if is archaic, as in 'an it please you'.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage is a union or partnership, and an alliance is a union, including one formed by marrying.

clue.text: Steer to leave this part of Africa

blocks.note: to con a ship is to steer it
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: A cattle herder is told to quit this region of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Steer looks like a young bull, but here it is a verb: conning is the naval word for directing a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Congo is a large region of central Africa named after its great river, and two states bear the name.

clue.text: Away with a king of Mercia

blocks.note: off means away, as in he's off
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old English king has gone away.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom of the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa ruled Mercia in the eighth century and is remembered for the earthwork Offa's Dyke.

clue.text: Its nice red strangely varying in hue

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters are set out in an odd order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A nice red colour that keeps oddly changing shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Iridescent surfaces, like soap bubbles or peacock feathers, show colours that shift with the angle of view.

clue.text: Leg bound to be damaged by a heavy stick

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's leg is certain to be hurt by a blow from a club.
explanation.walkthrough: Bound to be reads as 'certain to be'; bound is really part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A bludgeon is a short thick club with a weighted end, used as a weapon.

clue.text: Swimmer has a sort of jet type of shirt

blocks.note: a turbojet is a sort of jet engine
a T-shirt is a type of shirt

explanation.surface: A swimmer wears a shirt with a jet design on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Swimmer is crossword code for a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The turbot is a large flat fish of European seas, prized for its firm white flesh.
